implementation_notes: Swift key paths are the lens mechanism built into the language: `\Person.home.city` is a composed getter, `WritableKeyPath<Person, String>` is its setter, `appending(path:)` composes two key paths at runtime, and `value[keyPath: kp]` reads or writes through them - no optics library is needed for composition. Because structs are value types, applying a key path to an immutable value is one generic helper, `func with<T>(_ value: T, _ mutate: (inout T) -> Void) -> T` (or a `set(kp, v) -> (A) -> A` variant), which gives every writable field of every struct a lawful lens. A separate `Lens` type is justified only where key paths may not appear in the API - they are not Codable and cannot cross into Objective-C - or where a focus must be identified dynamically rather than by key path.
pitfalls: Only writable, non-private state yields a lens: `let` properties and `private(set) var` cannot form a `WritableKeyPath`, so key paths do not cover the whole model and the gap is discovered at compile time.
`set`/`with` copies the struct, but a class instance stored in that struct is copied by reference - "immutable update" then mutates shared state through the reference.
`ReferenceWritableKeyPath` writes through class instances instead of copying them, so composing a reference key path into a struct path quietly reintroduces mutable aliasing.
